company.name: Supabase
company.tagline: Borrowed substrate (30-year-old Postgres) + Launch Week as proactive-cadence E1 + pgvector six months ahead of the LLM wave
company.summary: Paul Copplestone (ex-Nimbus for Work, Entrepreneur First Singapore) and Ant Wilson (Imperial College London) started writing Supabase code in January 2020 and wrapped 30-year-old PostgreSQL in a modern developer-experience layer. A late-May 2020 Launch HN — 'Supabase (YC S20) – An open source Firebase alternative' — hit 1,120+ upvotes and was declared the second most-upvoted Launch HN in HN history at the time. They turned the post-YC ship-adrenaline withdrawal into Launch Week, a quarterly cadence that 94 other dev-tool companies eventually copied. In early 2023 they shipped pgvector six months ahead of mass LLM-app awareness — the cleanest single tech-narrative-upgrade timing decision in our case set. By 2024 every vibe-coding platform (Bolt, Lovable, v0, Cursor, Claude Code) was defaulting users to Supabase, in part because the Postgres substrate was pluckable — users could rip the stack out and keep their raw database. Six rounds in five years: Seed (Oct 2020) → A (Sep 2021) → B (Apr 2022) → C (Sep 2024) → D (Apr 2025, $200M @ $2B) → E (Oct 2025, $100M @ $5B). ARR is Sacra-estimated at ~$70M (Aug/Sep 2025, +250% YoY) — Supabase has not officially disclosed it. Reported ~$10B talks with GIC leading (April 2026) are not closed as of June 2026. The reusable lesson: when an industry-grade open-source asset already exists in your category, identifying it as your substrate is cheaper than building one — but only if you hire deep enough into that ecosystem (Postgres core contributors, NGINX co-founder, Vitess co-creator) for the borrowed framing to read as competence rather than thin wrapping.

phases.name: YC S20 + Launch HN + early OSS
Vibe-coding hyperscale (Series C → E → reported D+)

events.title: Supabase founded in Singapore
events.description: Paul Copplestone (CEO, ex-Nimbus for Work, Entrepreneur First Singapore) and Ant Wilson (CTO, Imperial College London MSc Software Engineering) start writing Supabase code as a Postgres-based open-source Firebase alternative. Pre-seed ~$100K from angels. The founding choice that makes everything possible: do not build a database — wrap the 30-year-old open-source one in modern developer experience.

events.title: 8 databases hosted
events.description: By April 2020 Supabase only hosts 8 databases — the slow early traction that almost killed the idea. Founders kept shipping; the substrate bet had not yet compounded.

events.title: Launch HN: Supabase (YC S20) — 1,120+ upvotes
events.description: Late-May 2020 HN post 'Supabase (YC S20) – An open source Firebase alternative' crosses 1,120+ upvotes. HN moderator dang upgrades it to the official Launch HN. Second most-upvoted Launch HN in Hacker News history at the time. Same-day Product Hunt: #3 of the day, 818 upvotes. Traffic spike crashes DigitalOcean limits — team migrates to AWS within hours. The reverse-positioning headline is the demo grammar — anyone burned by Firebase can reconstruct the full product promise from one line.

events.title: Auth ships
events.description: Supabase Auth ships, three months after Launch HN. Michael Seibel (YC) told Copplestone: stop thinking, ship it. Authentication becomes the most-adopted Supabase product among new customers and the first GoTrue-licensed sub-product.

events.title: Seed $6M — Coatue-led
events.description: $6M seed led by Coatue (Caryn Marooney, ex-Facebook VP Global Communications), with Y Combinator, Mozilla, and ~20 angels. Closed October 9, 2020; announced December 15. The non-obvious bet: Marooney is a marketing/comms VC, not a typical dev-tool VC. Coatue is pricing the founding team as a future developer-infrastructure brand, not as a GitHub-stars trajectory.

events.title: Seed announcement + Beta exit
events.description: Public seed announcement coincides with Beta exit. Supabase ends 2020 with ~3,100 databases hosted, up from 8 in April. TechCrunch's Frederic Lardinois carries the round.

events.title: Launch Week 1 — the format invented
events.description: First Launch Week (March 2021). Founders had missed the YC demo-day ship-adrenaline post-batch, so invented the format: ship one major feature every day for a week, quarterly. By 2024, launchweek.dev counts 126 Launch Weeks across 94 different dev-tool companies copying the format. The fourth sub-type of E1 (crisis-as-GTM): proactive-cadence — sustained product-output transparency rather than internal-state transparency (PostHog) or reactive postmortems (ElevenLabs).

events.title: Series A $30M — Coatue doubles down
events.description: $30M Series A led by Coatue (doubled down from seed). Caryn Marooney joins the board. Angels: Tom Preston-Werner (GitHub), Solomon Hykes (Docker), Guillermo Rauch (Vercel), Kurt Mackey (Fly), Alex Solomon (PagerDuty). Metrics: 50K databases, 40K developers, 4K Discord, top-15 fastest-growing OSS startup on GitHub for 5 consecutive quarters. Total raised: $36M.

events.title: Series B $80M — Felicis-led
events.description: $80M Series B led by Felicis Ventures (Aydin Senkut). Participants: Coatue, Lightspeed (new), Square Peg (new). Closed April 19, announced August 12. Metrics at announcement: 150K databases, 110K developers, 8K Discord, 36K GitHub stars, 37K Twitter. Total raised: $116M.

events.title: Six-product platform live
events.description: By mid-2022 Supabase has all six core products live: Database (Postgres), Auth (GoTrue), Storage (S3-backed), Edge Functions (Deno runtime), Realtime (Elixir / Phoenix Channels), Vector (pgvector groundwork). Each is usable standalone. Narrative shifts from 'open source Firebase alternative' to 'Postgres-based developer platform.'

events.title: pgvector + AI Toolkit ship
events.description: Supabase becomes one of the earliest managed-Postgres providers to ship pgvector for storing embeddings. AI toolkit includes Python client, embedding generation in Edge Functions, and integrations with OpenAI / Hugging Face / LangChain. Pre-positions Supabase as the default backend for the LLM-app wave — roughly six months before mass developer awareness of the LLM-app stack arrives.

events.title: Quivr viral pgvector case study
events.description: Stan Girard ships Quivr (chat-with-documents 'second brain') in a single afternoon, pushes to GitHub, viral tweet. Picks Supabase Vector over Pinecone / Chroma / Weaviate / Faiss because vector embeddings + relational data on one substrate beats integrating five vendors. First widely-shared production pgvector case.

events.title: Vibe-coding inflection — Bolt + Lovable adopt Supabase as default
events.description: Bolt.new and Lovable both adopt Supabase as their default backend. v0 (Vercel) adds Supabase as the default database prompt for AI-generated apps. Cursor and Claude Code integrations follow. User sign-up rate begins doubling every ~3 months on vibe-coding adoption. Supabase pays zero CAC for the entire AI-app distribution layer.

events.title: Series C $80M @ ~$765M — Peak XV + Craft co-lead
events.description: $80M Series C led by Peak XV + Craft Ventures, with Avra Capital (Anu Hariharan, ex-YC Growth, new) + Coatue + Felicis + YC. Up round, valuation undisclosed (PitchBook later estimates ~$765M post-money). Metrics disclosed: ~900K signups in 4 years; 40% of latest YC batch on Supabase; ~10% of active databases are AI workloads; enterprise customers include GitHub Next, Meta, Netflix, Microsoft. Total raised: $196M.

events.title: ~$30M ARR end-2024 (Sacra estimate)
events.description: Sacra estimates Supabase reaches ~$30M ARR by end-2024 — quietly compounding through vibe-coding adoption. ARR not officially disclosed by Supabase. taptwicedigital's alternative lower estimate of $16.8M for 2024 suggests measurement difference (paid Cloud only vs total including enterprise).

events.title: Series D $200M @ $2B — Accel-led + Wānaka doorstep story
events.description: $200M Series D led by Accel at $2B post-money. Origin story: Accel's Gonzalo Mocorrea showed up at Copplestone's New Zealand doorstep in Wānaka unannounced; Arun Mathew followed across 24 hours of travel. Supabase was not actively raising. Angels: Kevin Weil (OpenAI CPO), Guillermo Rauch (Vercel CEO), Taylor Otwell (Laravel). Metrics: 2M developers, 3.5M databases, sign-up rate doubled every 3 months on vibe coding. Total raised: $398M.

events.title: Launch Week 15
events.description: 15th Launch Week (July 14–18, 2025), 4+ years after the format was invented. Includes hackathon + global meetups. Cadence confirms the format scales without dilution; quarterly rhythm holds at >$2B-valuation scale.

events.title: Bolt Cloud + Lovable Cloud — first structural competitive threat
events.description: Bolt Cloud launches August 2025, followed by Lovable Cloud, both letting vibe-coding platforms monetize backends directly rather than handing users off to Supabase. Sacra flags this as the first structural disintermediation risk for Supabase — the vibe-coding distribution layer may not stay free forever.

events.title: ~$70M ARR + 4M developers (Sacra estimate)
events.description: Sacra estimates Supabase ARR at ~$70M Aug/Sep 2025 — 250% YoY from $30M end-2024. User growth +700% YoY. 4M+ developers, 100K+ customers, 3.5M+ databases. Still not officially disclosed by Supabase.

events.title: Series E $100M @ $5B + Multigres announcement — eight stories one cycle
events.description: $100M Series E at $5B pre-money, co-led by Accel + Peak XV. Figma is only new institutional investor — all other existing investors return (YC, Coatue, Felicis, Craft, Square Peg). Bundled with: $1M planned community co-investment round, hire of Sugu Sougoumarane (Vitess co-creator) to lead Multigres / Vitess-for-Postgres enterprise scale, the every-round 25% employee secondary continues. Total raised: ~$500M. Eight independently quotable stories in one news cycle.

events.title: Era-defining database thesis published
events.description: Accel publishes 'Supabase's Series E: An Era-Defining Database' thesis post; Coatue's Caryn Marooney frames the bet as 'becoming the backend for everyone, from startups to demanding enterprise workloads.' Cements vibe-coding-substrate-plus-enterprise narrative.

events.title: 100K GitHub stars
events.description: Main supabase/supabase repo crosses 100,000 GitHub stars — top-100 most-starred repo on GitHub. Doubled in ~2 years (from ~50K in 2023). Concrete substrate-tier validation.

events.title: $10B talks reported (not closed)
events.description: The Information scoops: Supabase in advanced talks to raise ~$500M at ~$10B valuation, led by GIC (Singapore sovereign wealth fund — Copplestone's original Entrepreneur First Singapore base). Would 2x valuation in 6 months. Round NOT yet closed as of June 2026; coverage is media-scoop confidence only.

platforms.name: GitHub
platforms.role: The Apache 2.0 core itself plus pgvector lineage
platforms.description: supabase/supabase main repository under Apache 2.0 (Storage / GoTrue / Realtime separately MIT). Crossed 100K stars April 2, 2026, top-100 most-starred repo on GitHub. Where AI coding tools hit when generating Supabase scaffolds. The borrowed-substrate framing is verifiable here — Postgres core extensions, pgvector, and the realtime Elixir layer all live in public.
platforms.catalyst: Late-May 2020 Launch HN linked supabase/supabase as the canonical artifact. Eighteen-month compounding to 19K stars at Series A (Sep 2021); 36K at Series B (Aug 2022); ~50K by end 2023; 100K April 2, 2026.
platforms.whenItWorks: When the open-source license is permissive (Apache 2.0 or MIT) and self-hosting is genuinely achievable. Pluckability is the value, not lock-in.
platforms.whenItDoesnt: AGPL or BSL killing the substrate effect (Elastic, MongoDB, HashiCorp). Supabase chose Apache 2.0 deliberately for the same reason Vercel chose MIT for Next.js.

platforms.name: Hacker News
platforms.description: The late-May 2020 Launch HN ('Supabase (YC S20) – An open source Firebase alternative') hit 1,120+ upvotes and was declared by HN moderator dang the second most-upvoted Launch HN at the time. Every subsequent major release (pgvector, multi-product GA, Series D, Series E, 100K stars milestone) surfaced on HN's front page. Comment threads stress-test claims and become the discoverable artifact for the next two years of buyer research.
platforms.catalyst: Late-May 2020 Launch HN post — declared a Launch HN by dang after a user posted it organically. 1,120+ upvotes; second most-upvoted Launch HN in HN history at the time. Traffic spike crashed DigitalOcean limits; team migrated to AWS within hours.
platforms.whenItWorks: When the launch has genuine technical novelty (here: SQL + realtime + open source + self-hostable in one container) and the headline collapses the reverse-positioning frame into one line.
platforms.whenItDoesnt: When the post is PR-styled. HN punishes promotional content quickly and the comment thread becomes a credibility risk.

platforms.name: X (Twitter)
platforms.description: Paul Copplestone (@kiwicopple) and Ant Wilson (@antwilson) run the daily build-in-public surface. Paul is the louder strategic voice; Ant the quieter technical leg. Every Launch Week ships its daily reveals first on X. The @supabase company account amplifies. Total followers in the hundreds of thousands by 2025; tier-1 dev-twitter status.
platforms.catalyst: No single tweet. Continuous founder presence since 2020, with Launch Week serving as the regular amplification event. The Apr 22, 2025 Wānaka-doorstep Series D narrative landed first on X before Fortune.
platforms.whenItWorks: When the founder can sustain technical depth and post the same product cadence the team is shipping — substrate underneath, not theater.
platforms.whenItDoesnt: Daily founder posting devolves into thought leadership without operating substance. The Launch Week cadence prevents this — there is always real product to point at.

platforms.name: Launch Week (proactive cadence)
platforms.description: Invented March 2021 as the founders' response to losing YC ship-adrenaline. Quarterly cadence: ship one major feature every day for a week, every quarter. Cross-platform synchronous blast — HN, Product Hunt, X, email, Discord. Engineer-as-marketer model: the engineer shipping the feature writes the launch copy. Fifteen completed Launch Weeks by July 2025. By 2024, launchweek.dev counts 126 Launch Weeks across 94 different dev-tool companies copying the format. The fourth E1 sub-pattern — proactive-cadence — alongside reactive (ElevenLabs), proactive-safety (Anthropic), and proactive-transparency (PostHog handbook).
platforms.catalyst: March 2021 — Launch Week 1. The format that took over dev-tools marketing. Most copyable variant of the E1 sub-types for product-led companies without research labs.
platforms.whenItWorks: When the team can ship five legitimate features a week, four times a year, without padding. The format is unforgiving — bad Launch Weeks are visible as bad Launch Weeks.
platforms.whenItDoesnt: Marketing-team-driven Launch Weeks without engineer authorship produce padded news cycles. The cadence becomes a calendar event, not a product cycle, and the trust signal inverts.

platforms.name: Y Combinator (S20 + ongoing customer pipeline)
platforms.role: Founding accelerator + perpetual YC-batch customer pipeline
platforms.description: Supabase is YC S20 — the first all-remote batch forced by COVID. YC participated in every primary round through Series E. By Series C (Sep 2024), 40% of the latest YC batch was on Supabase — every batch produces 200+ new dev-tool buyers, and Supabase's open-source default makes adoption frictionless. The YC blog and Michael Seibel's early 'stop thinking, ship it' counsel show up in founder retellings.
platforms.catalyst: Summer 2020 YC batch (S20) — the all-remote batch that let Singapore-based Copplestone and London-based Wilson form a remote-first team from Day 0. Pre-COVID, that pairing might not have happened.
platforms.whenItWorks: When the YC network is also your customer base — Supabase's developer-tool category puts a steady-state percentage of every batch into the funnel. 40% of W24 / S24 batches on Supabase is the legible version of this.
platforms.whenItDoesnt: If your buyer is enterprise-only or non-technical, the YC customer-pipeline value is much weaker.

platforms.name: Podcasts (episodic founder-as-IP)
platforms.description: Paul Copplestone runs ~10 long-form podcast appearances across the funding ladder: Accel 'Spotlight On' (with Arun Mathew + Gonzalo Mocorrea), TechCrunch Equity, Felicis founder interview, Changelog #599, Scaling DevTools, Evil Martians Dev Propulsion Labs, PodRocket. Each hits a specific strategic decision — turning down enterprise contracts to protect product vision, why database migration doesn't work, global remote hiring from Day 0, the Nicki Minaj naming origin. Episodic density rather than Vercel-style daily X presence.
platforms.catalyst: Accel 'Spotlight On' episode (post-Series D, 2025) — three-way conversation that turns the Wānaka doorstep story into the canonical Supabase founder narrative.
platforms.whenItWorks: When the founder has substantive, non-overlapping strategy material for each appearance. Each episode must be load-bearing on a different decision — otherwise the founder becomes podcast wallpaper.
platforms.whenItDoesnt: Repeating the same three anecdotes across 10 podcasts. The episodic E2 only works when the operator has enough lived decisions to keep each appearance fresh.
